It’s time to answer our Weekly Tokimeki Question!✨️ What color sparks joy for you?

For Marie, it’s white. “Wearing white calms me and refreshes me, and it feels like it’s easier for me to hear my own voice at the moment.”

This week’s question may feel simple, but it’s an entryway to start noticing the things around you more! 🎨

① Take a moment to ask yourself: What color sparks joy for you? What is the first color that comes to mind?
② As you enjoy your day, keep that color in mind, so you can find moments of joy you may have never noticed before! You can even wear clothes that are that color to experience and notice how it makes you feel!
③ Share the color or colors that give you the feeling of tokimeki in the comments below in either the form of a photo or comment! We’ll showcase your photos and comments in a feature post!👇️❤️

#artoftokimeki #tokimeki #prompt #journalprompt #personaldevelopment

When we think about tokimeki, there are 3 main circles that you should try to keep in balance to make joy more sustainable in your life. They are：

1. Your Joy Circle: Understanding Your Joy
Finding joy for yourself is essential. It is what drives you forward. When you are fulfilled and happy, your capacity to contribute increases, and when self-care becomes possible, it becomes easier to thrive and share.

2. Your Social Circle: To Share & Amplify
Joy multiplies when shared. Understanding what sparks joy for those you care about creates stronger bonds and mutual support. When you have social joy, even personal achievements can feel more exciting.

3. Your Value Circle: What You Bring Beyond Yourself. What You Bring to the World
Through work, art, service, or innovation, contribute to the world. With external value, the practice can become much more sustainable as a lifestyle.

Your personal joy circle, your social circle, and your value circle.
All three together to create a more joyful life for you, your people, and the world.

✨Follow us as we share practices, rituals, prompts, etc. to learn how!

#tokimeki #artoftokimeki #ritual #joy #community

When you fill your heart with joy, it makes it more sustainable to share that joy with others. It begins by asking yourself what truly matters. When you make space for the things that bring you genuine joy, you naturally have more energy, presence, and kindness that you can then share with the people around you💛

The joy you cultivate within yourself becomes the joy you can share with others in a sustainable way!✨

👉Save and repost this post as a reminder to yourself and others to fill your own heart with Tokimeki and joy which in the end can then expand to the people around you, and then to the world!🌎

#artoftokimeki #tokimeki #sparkjoy #quote #inspirationalquote

In the age of AI, what will matter most about being human?

We've spent decades valuing IQ (Intelligence Quotient), and more recently, EQ (Emotional Quotient). But what if the next quotient that defines our humanity is TQ: the Tokimeki Quotient?

Takumi Kawahara, CEO of KonMari Media Inc. (and Marie Kondo's husband), shares that TQ is our ability to recognize and choose what truly sparks joy by honing our sensitivity to what matters most to us.

In a world where AI can help us think faster and do more, our uniquely human ability to sense what is meaningful becomes even more valuable. When we learn to trust our innate sense of what sparks joy, we can make decisions with greater clarity, confidence, and alignment with the life we want to live.

Here at @artoftokimeki, we'll be exploring the philosophy behind TQ and sharing practical ways to better understand and cultivate your own Tokimeki Quotient.

What do you think of this idea? We'd love to hear your thoughts below.👇

#artoftokimeki #tokimeki #sparkjoy #TQ #philosophy

Welcome back to the Weekly Tokimeki Question! This week we’re reflecting on the small joys of your day! ❤️

Sometimes life feels too busy to reflect on the good things that happened, but we hope this is a gentle reminder to look back at your day and appreciate even the smallest things! It can truly change your perspective on your day ✨

📌Try this out with us:
① Take a moment to close your eyes and take a deep breath.
② Slowly reflect on your day. What is one joy-sparking thing in your life that you want to thank?
③ Write it down in your journal or in the comments!
④ We’d love for you all to share your little joys of the day and spread Tokimeki together!

We’ll be sharing some of your answers in a community highlight post soon, so don’t forget to share your little joys with us!👇
